MAPMYINDIA.why: Below its IPO price after a sharp 2026 slide: it fell 36% from a January high to a 32-month low in February, then dropped about 7% on 5 August after JM Financial cut earnings estimates and downgraded it post Q1 FY27. Q3 FY26 profit fell nearly 42% and revenue fell over 18% on delayed government projects and spend on navigation and HD-mapping software. FY26 growth was only about 1-2%.
MAPMYINDIA.outlook: Order book was about ₹1,770 crore in December 2025 (₹1,500 crore in March 2025), and management aims for ₹1,000 crore revenue by FY28. One analysis expects growth to return to 20%+ in FY27 led by government and IoT; Q1 FY27 IoT revenue rose 75% but the maps business was flat. Software stocks generally were also weak.

AGSTRA.why: Collapsed to near zero after a debt default. Crisil and India Ratings downgraded it in February 2025, the stock fell about 62% within weeks, all four independent directors resigned, and an operational creditor filed an insolvency petition. The company and units owe about ₹719 crore to creditors including SBI and Axis Bank.
AGSTRA.outlook: Reportedly in insolvency resolution since August 2025 and late filing FY26 audited accounts. The NCLT admission order was not found, so check exchange filings. In an insolvency, equity holders are usually last in line, so recovery looks remote.

DELHIVERY.why: Operations improved but the stock has stayed below its IPO price. Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26% to ₹2,850 crore and EBITDA rose 80% to ₹210 crore, helped by the Ecom Express purchase (about ₹1,407 crore, completed July 2025), which lifted express parcel volumes 73%. Profit was flat at about ₹72 crore and the shares fell about 5% on results day because the valuation is very high (about 226x earnings).
DELHIVERY.outlook: Management guides to 15-20% annual volume growth and 16-18% service margins for two years. Motilal Oswal is Buy with a ₹580 target and sees revenue and EBITDA compounding 13% and 33% over FY26-28; Trendlyne's consensus target was about ₹565. Risks: integration costs (Q2 FY26 loss of ₹50 crore), Amazon and Flipkart building their own logistics, and the premium valuation.

EMUDHRA.why: The gain comes from steady growth in digital signatures and trust services as banks, brokerages and fintechs move to paperless processes (its emSigner platform), plus acquisitions (Cryptas). Realisation per signature is thin, about ₹2. Price sources disagreed, so the exact path in 2026 could not be pinned down.
EMUDHRA.outlook: Management guided 25-30% revenue growth for FY26, roughly 15-20% organic and 10% from acquisitions. A November 2025 broker note was Buy with a ₹710 target and projected revenue and profit CAGRs of 31.8% and 41.3% for FY25-27, but that is dated. Risks cited: cyber security incidents, losing a key client, regulatory changes.

SYRMA.why: Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 67% to ₹1,589 crore and profit more than doubled to about ₹106 crore, led by auto (+78%), consumer (+68%) and IT and railways (+199%). The shares roughly doubled from a January 2026 low. Drivers: customs-duty relief on electronics manufacturing machinery to March 2029, a joint venture with Japan's Kaga Electronics, the Elcome defence acquisition, and a mix shift away from low-margin consumer work.
SYRMA.outlook: Order book about ₹6,770 crore (up 23%). Management guides to 35%+ revenue growth and a 10.5-11% EBITDA margin for FY27 and says it expects to beat revenue guidance. ICICI Direct is Buy with a ₹1,680 target (July 2026); Antique targets ₹1,601. Risks: supply-chain disruption, margin swings, and the sharp run-up.

TRACXN.why: Stalled growth: operating revenue stayed flat while costs, mainly staff, rose, leading to losses. Subscription revenue was unchanged over nine months of FY26, new accounts added in Q2 fell 44% to 113, international revenue fell 11% and average deal size dropped from ₹5.2 lakh to ₹4.3 lakh. Market cap fell from ₹559 crore to ₹369 crore during Q3 FY26. India is the bright spot (accounts +43%, revenue +14% in 9M FY26).
TRACXN.outlook: Management plans to grow the India sales team from 25 to about 40 and the US-focused team from under 10 to about 25, and to use AI to speed data production. FY27 guidance was not found, so the turnaround is unproven.

KAYNES.why: Up about 5.5x from the IPO price, but it fell about 25% in three sessions in May 2026 after weak Q4 FY26 results: revenue and operating cash flow missed estimates and management trimmed its FY27 growth outlook; Elara downgraded it to Accumulate. The sources for this are thin and republished, so verify against the filings.
KAYNES.outlook: The recovery case rests on its semiconductor packaging and test (OSAT) plant. Management says it could add meaningful revenue once running, but timing is uncertain. Nothing on later quarters was found.

KFINTECH.why: Revenue growth has been strong but profit is lagging. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to ₹356.5 crore (helped by the Ascent acquisition, consolidated from Q3 FY26) while profit fell about 2.6% to ₹75.2 crore as EBITDA margin dropped to 34.2% from 41.5%. The core mutual fund business grew only about 7%. The shares jumped 11% in July 2026 on upbeat management commentary on growth, profitability and international expansion.
KFINTECH.outlook: Brokers are positive: one has Buy with a ₹1,150 target and Trendlyne's consensus was about ₹1,107 in August 2026. Whether margins recover is the key question, and at around 43x earnings the valuation is rich.

AVALON.why: Strong operating run: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 50% to ₹484 crore, profit rose 145%, EBITDA margin was 12%, and FY26 profit rose 78% to ₹113 crore. Growth rides India's electronics-manufacturing push, a strong order book and new programme ramp-ups.
AVALON.outlook: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 26-30% (from 24-27%) and targets doubling revenue to ₹3,200 crore by FY29. Industry data cited: India EMS growing at a 27% CAGR and India's share of global electronics manufacturing rising from 4% to 10% by 2030. Risks: raw-material prices and US operations. Price figures in the sources were inconsistent.
